title: Read, Build, and Write About Things
summary: Express ownership by placing the possessor after the thing and by using se pou.

sketchBlocks.title: Put the owner after the thing
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
In a simple possessive noun phrase, the possessor comes after the thing:

- **machin mwen** — my car
- **kaye ou** — your notebook
- **fanmi li** — his/her family

The same personal forms from Module 3 now show ownership.

tryItExercises.title: Build a new possessive phrase
tryItExercises.prompt: Arrange the Kreyòl phrase for “my book.”
tryItExercises.hint: Put the owner after the thing.

help.hint_1: Use the Kreyòl pattern from this lesson.
help.hint_2: Use the pattern you just learned.

sketchBlocks.title: machin mwen an
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
When the phrase is definite, the definite marker still comes at the end:

**machin mwen an** — my car / the car that is mine

The pattern is: **thing + possessor + definite marker**.

tryItExercises.title: Build another definite possessive phrase
tryItExercises.prompt: Arrange the definite Kreyòl phrase for “my book.”
tryItExercises.hint: Use thing + possessor + final definite marker.

help.hint_1: Use the Kreyòl pattern from this lesson.
help.hint_2: Use the pattern you just learned.

sketchBlocks.title: Sa se pou mwen
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
You can also express ownership with **se pou**:

- **Sa se pou mwen.** — This/that is mine / for me.
- **Liv la se pou li.** — The book is his/hers.

This pattern is useful when identifying who an object belongs to.

tryItExercises.title: Say who it belongs to
tryItExercises.prompt: Say “This is yours / for you.” in Kreyòl.
tryItExercises.hint: Keep Sa se pou and change the person.
